claim: Carcinogenic HPVs cause nearly all cervical cancers.
source: Roughly a dozen 'high-risk' HPV types cause nearly all cervical cancers, a large majority of other anogenital cancers, and about half of all oropharyngeal cancers (Graham, 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Graham, 2017

claim: High-risk HPV types cause a large majority of other anogenital cancers.
source: Roughly a dozen 'high-risk' HPV types cause nearly all cervical cancers, a large majority of other anogenital cancers, and about half of all oropharyngeal cancers (Graham, 2017).

claim: High-risk HPV types cause about half of all oropharyngeal cancers.

evidence: Supported by citation to Graham, 2017

claim: HPV E6 and E7 oncogenes inactivate the tumor suppressor proteins p53 and Rb, respectively.
source: The carcinogenic effects of these small circular double-stranded DNA viruses are primarily dependent on the expression of the E6 and E7 oncogenes which, among a wide range of other functions, inactivate the tumor suppressor proteins p53 and Rb, respectively (Rosty et al., 2005; Crook et al., 1991; Mirabello et al., 2017; DeCaprio, 2014; Barbosa et al., 1990).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: Polyomavirus T antigens perform many of the same functions as papillomavirus oncoproteins.
source: In particular, polyomavirus T antigens perform many of the same functions as papillomavirus oncoproteins and are similarly oncogenic in cellular and animal models (Moens and Macdonald, 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Moens and Macdonald, 2019

claim: MCPyV has been identified as an etiological factor in Merkel cell carcinoma.
source: MCPyV has been identified as an etiological factor in a rare skin cancer, Merkel cell carcinoma (Feng et al., 2008; Shuda et al., 2008; Kassem et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: Kidney recipients who develop BKPyV viremia or BKPyV-induced nephropathy after transplant are at increased risk of bladder cancer.
source: Several case reports have described the detection of BKPyV in bladder cancers arising in transplant recipients, and kidney recipients who develop BKPyV viremia or BKPyV-induced nephropathy (BKVN) after transplant are at increased risk of bladder cancer (Gupta et al., 2018; Vajdic and van Leeuwen, 2009; Li et al., 2021; Papadimitriou et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: Bladder cancers exhibit somatic point mutations that are largely attributable to the activity of APOBEC3 family cytosine deaminases.
source: Similar to HPV-induced cervical and oropharyngeal cancers, bladder cancers exhibit somatic point mutations that are largely attributable to the activity of APOBEC3 family cytosine deaminases (Robertson et al., 2017; Burns et al., 2013; Roberts et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: APOBEC3 enzymes normally function as innate immune defenses against viruses by deaminating cytosines in single-stranded DNA.
source: These enzymes normally function as innate immune defenses against viruses by deaminating cytosines in single-stranded DNA, leading to hypermutation of the viral genome (Poulain et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Poulain et al., 2020

claim: APOBEC3A and APOBEC3B are upregulated in response to the expression of HPV E6 and E7.
source: APOBEC3A and APOBEC3B are upregulated in response to the expression of HPV E6 and E7, and APOBEC3A can restrict HPV replication (Mori et al., 2017; Warren et al., 2017; Ahasan et al., 2015; Warren et al., 2015b; Vieira et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: APOBEC3A can restrict HPV replication.
source: APOBEC3A and APOBEC3B are upregulated in response to the expression of HPV E6 and E7, and APOBEC3A can restrict HPV replication (Mori et al., 2017; Warren et al., 2017; Ahasan et al., 2015; Warren et al., 2015b; Vieira et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

evidence: Supported by multiple citations
